what.text: L-arginine is an amino acid found in food. The body uses it to make nitric oxide, a messenger that relaxes blood vessels, including those in the penis. That is the reason it has been studied for erectile dysfunction (ED).

src.label: Chen J, et al. BJU Int 1999
Klotz T, et al. Urol Int 1999

what.text: Under US law, a product containing an amino acid and meant to supplement the diet can be sold as a dietary supplement. Amino acids are also permitted as food additives for listed uses.

what.text: As a drug, FDA has approved arginine only as R-Gene 10, an injection into a vein used as a test of the pituitary gland’s growth hormone reserve.

what.text: L-arginine is not FDA approved for ED. As a supplement, it is not reviewed by FDA before sale.

research.text: Trials of L-arginine for ED are small, mostly 30 to 100 men, lasting 17 days to 3 months, and results differ. A 2019 meta-analysis pooled 10 randomized trials with 540 men; several included arginine combined with other substances. Many newer trials test arginine added to PDE5 drugs such as tadalafil.

research.title: High dose in physically caused ED, 1999

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, after a 2-week placebo run-in
questionnaires, sex diary, penile blood flow, nitric oxide breakdown products in blood and urine

research.found: 9 of 29 men on L-arginine and 2 of 17 on placebo reported a clear improvement. All objective measures, including penile blood flow, were unchanged. The men who improved had low nitric oxide markers at the start.

src.label: Chen J, et al. BJU Int 1999

research.title: Low dose in mixed-type ED, 1999

facts.v: 32 men with ED of mixed causes; 30 completed
two 17-day courses with a 7-day break; 500 mg three times a day

research.found: 5 men improved clearly on L-arginine and 6 on placebo. There was no statistical difference. No side effects were linked to L-arginine.

src.label: Klotz T, et al. Urol Int 1999

research.title: High dose in vascular ED, 3 months

facts.v: 98 men with ED from poor blood flow (51 L-arginine, 47 placebo)
erectile function score (IIEF-6) and penile artery blood flow by ultrasound

research.found: The erectile function score and penile blood flow rose with L-arginine. 74% moved to a milder ED category, but only 24%, mostly men with mild ED at the start, reached scores in the normal range.

src.label: Menafra D, et al. J Endocrinol Invest 2022

research.title: Pooled analysis of 10 trials, 540 men

facts.v: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials against placebo or no treatment
540 men with mild to moderate ED
1,500 to 5,000 mg arginine alone or combined with other substances
improvement rate, erectile function scores, side effects

research.found: Arginine was linked to more improvement than placebo (odds ratio 3.37). Side effects were reported in 8.3% on arginine and 2.3% on placebo, none severe. Doses and lengths varied between trials.

src.label: Rhim HC, et al. J Sex Med 2019 (meta-analysis)

research.text: ClinicalTrials.gov lists 7 studies for “arginine erectile,” including a completed Phase II dose-finding trial in 140 prostate cancer survivors and several trials of arginine with tadalafil.

us.text: L-arginine is not FDA approved for ED. It can be sold as a dietary supplement, which FDA does not approve or review for safety or effectiveness before sale. Its only FDA-approved drug use is R-Gene 10, a diagnostic injection. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: amino acids are dietary ingredients under the law that defines dietary supplements. FDA does not have the authority to approve dietary supplements before they are marketed.

side.text: In the ED trials, side effects were usually mild and reported in a minority of men. In one heart-attack trial, more people on L-arginine died. As a supplement, it is not reviewed by FDA before sale.

items.text: side effects in 8.3% on arginine versus 2.3% on placebo across 10 trials, none severe.

items.text: in a 2006 randomized trial of 153 people after a first heart attack, 6 of those on L-arginine (8.6%) died within 6 months versus none on placebo. The safety committee stopped enrollment.
